elements.label: Figure 4.2
elements.description: Scatter plot with a fitted upward-sloping trend line. X-axis: 'Log Real GDP Per Capita at PPP', ticks 6 to 12. Y-axis: 'Learning-adjusted years of education', ticks 0 to 14 in steps of 2. Most points are teal, and a set of comparator countries is highlighted in orange with labels and leader lines. Labeled points, approximate readings: Singapore ~11.5 log GDP, ~12.8 years; Vietnam ~9.1, ~10.6 (teal); Malaysia ~10.8, ~8.1; Thailand ~10.2, ~6.5; Philippines ~8.6, ~7.9; Cambodia ~8.3, ~6.9; Indonesia ~9.4, ~6.3; Lao PDR ~9.1, ~4.0; Myanmar ~8.7, ~6.2. Many unlabeled teal points cluster at log GDP ~10.5 to 11 with learning-adjusted years ~10 to 12, and at log GDP ~7 to 9 with values ~4 to 8. Source note below the chart: 'Source: World Bank staff calculations using HCI data sheet, WDI.' The visible pattern is a clear positive relationship between income and learning-adjusted years of schooling, with Vietnam sitting above the trend line for its income level.
